name: Arjun
primary_meaning: Arjun (Sanskrit अर्जुन, Arjuna) is a male name meaning “white, bright, clear” or “silver”. It is the name of Arjuna, the great archer-hero of the Mahabharata, third of the five Pandava brothers and the friend and disciple of Krishna in the Bhagavad Gita.
literal_meaning: White, clear, bright (Sanskrit árjuna); as a noun, silver
meaning_explanation: Sanskrit árjuna is an adjective meaning “white; clear; bright” and, as a neuter noun, “silver”. It goes back to the Proto-Indo-European root *h₂erǵ-, “white, shining”, the same root as Latin argentum, “silver”. Monier-Williams gives the meaning of Arjuna as white, clear or silver. The tree Terminalia arjuna also bears the name.

etymology.morphology: Sanskrit adjective árjuna, “white, bright”; Hindi Arjun drops the final short a.
etymology.explanation: From Sanskrit árjuna, inherited from Proto-Indo-European *h₂erǵ-, “white, shining; silver”; cognate with Latin argentum.
etymology.false_etymology_warning: Arjun does not mean “dark one”; the Sanskrit word means the opposite — white or bright.

origin.explanation: Sanskrit, from the Mahabharata; Arjun is the modern Hindi and Marathi form of the epic name. Arjuna also appears in Indonesian (Javanese and Balinese) tradition.

religion.status: Name of the hero of the Mahabharata and the Bhagavad Gita
religion.explanation: Arjuna is the third of the five Pandava brothers, son of Kunti and the god Indra. Before the Kurukshetra war Krishna, acting as his charioteer, gives him the teaching recorded in the Bhagavad Gita.
religion.vedic: Sanskrit árjuna, “bright”, occurs in the Rigveda (6.9.1).

cultural.meaning: Arjuna is the model of skill, discipline and devotion — the archer who won Draupadi at her swayamvara.
cultural.impact: Arjuna is known by many epithets that are also names, such as Dhananjaya (“conqueror of wealth”), Gudakesha (“conqueror of sleep”), Vijaya (“victorious”) and Partha.

items: The name of the central hero of the Mahabharata, composed over centuries in ancient India.
Also attested in Old Javanese, where arjuna means “white”.
history.person: Arjuna, third of the Pandava brothers in the Mahabharata.
history.event: Kurukshetra war and the Bhagavad Gita

modern_usage: A widely used boy's name in India and the Indian diaspora.

pronunciation.note: Sanskrit Arjuna has a final short a and Vedic accent on the first syllable (árjuna).

variant_notes: Arjuna is the Sanskrit and epic form; Arjunan is a South Indian form.

faq.a: Arjun comes from Sanskrit árjuna, meaning “white, bright, clear” or “silver”.
No. The Sanskrit word means white or bright; “dark” is a common error.

faq.q: Who is Arjuna in the Mahabharata?
faq.a: The third of the five Pandava brothers, son of Kunti and Indra, the greatest archer of the epic and Krishna's friend.

faq.q: What is Arjun's connection to the Bhagavad Gita?
faq.a: The Gita is Krishna's teaching to Arjuna on the battlefield of Kurukshetra, with Krishna serving as his charioteer.

faq.q: What are other names of Arjuna?
faq.a: Dhananjaya, Gudakesha, Vijaya, Partha, Savyasachi and Kiriti are among his epithets.

faq.q: What is the root of Arjun?
faq.a: The Proto-Indo-European root *h₂erǵ-, “white, shining”, also found in Latin argentum, “silver”.
